title: Xylem-Mediated Calcium Translocation Kinetics and Root-Pressure Driven Guttation Steering
description: PhD research detailing mechanosensitive Ca2+ ion channel transport, xylem sap mass flow, and nighttime VPD suppression to eliminate localized physiological disorders in Solanaceae.
image_caption: Xylem pressure transducer setup monitoring nocturnal root pressure and guttation droplet formation.
overview: Calcium (Ca²⁺) is an immobile nutrient transported exclusively through the xylem via transpirational pull and root pressure mass flow. Under high VPD conditions (> 1.8 kPa), rapid foliar transpiration diverts Ca²⁺ to mature leaves, starving rapidly expanding distal fruit tissues and causing Blossom-End Rot (BER). This paper formulates a nocturnal root-pressure steering protocol: by lowering air temperature to 18°C and reducing nighttime VPD to < 0.2 kPa for 3 hours before dawn, positive root xylem pressure (> 0.15 MPa) forces Ca²⁺-rich sap directly into non-transpiring fruit apices.

climate_strategy.strategy: Execute pre-dawn humidity boost (RH > 92%, VPD < 0.2 kPa) combined with zero substrate drainage to induce root guttation. Monitor Calcium Nitrate [PubChem CID 24963] concentration in drainage sap.

crop_steering.intro: Micro-climatic control of xylem sap velocity and calcium partitioning.

vegetative_triggers.irrigation: Ca²⁺ concentration: 4.5 mM, Substrate moisture: 75% at night

generative_triggers.irrigation: Ca²⁺ concentration: 5.5 mM, Nighttime root pressure push

fertigation.intro: Divalent ion competition management (Ca²⁺ vs. K⁺ / Mg²⁺ / NH4⁺).
fertigation.vegetative_phase: Balance Calcium Nitrate [PubChem CID 24963] against Magnesium Sulfate [PubChem CID 24083] at a molar ratio of 2.5:1 (Ca 4.5 mM, Mg 1.8 mM) to prevent competitive ion antagonism at root plasma membrane ZIP transporters.
fertigation.generative_phase: Restrict root-zone Ammonium Nitrate [PubChem CID 22985] below 0.5 mM during rapid fruit swell.

references.text: Xylem transport and calcium distribution in CEA tomatoes under controlled micro-climate.
